# Run a package's gate with speca and reuse a result that passed

## Intent

The gate that decides whether a task or a branch may land is the package's
own `linter` and `all_tests` commands. Today a model runs them by hand, after
every task, and keeps the results in its head: it runs trees that were already
checked, nothing measures what a run costs, and the bookkeeping differs from
run to run. `speca` runs the gate instead. One call runs the commands, reuses
a passing result for a tree that was already checked, keeps the output out of
the model's context, measures the run, and answers with one JSON verdict. A
second call sums a package's runs for the merge commit. The gate is the same
for a person, an unattended run and a repair, and its cost is on record.

## Goals

- **The gate is a command.** `speca <package> --gate task|full` runs the
  package's `linter`, then its `all_tests`, without a shell, stops at the
  first command that fails, and answers with one verdict: `pass`, `fail` or
  `not_run`.
- **A tree that passed is not checked again.** A gate whose working tree,
  level, commands and environment match a recorded pass returns that pass
  without running anything, and says which commit and time it came from. A
  failure is never reused.
- **The clean-environment run is a flag.** `--clean-env` runs the gate with
  an empty `HOME`, no global or system git configuration and
  `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
- **A failure is readable without a log.** Every command's full output goes
  to a log file outside the repository; the verdict names the file and holds
  the last 40 lines of a failing command.
- **Gate cost is measured.** Every run records its seconds, and a full gate
  whose output is Go's keeps its five slowest test packages.
- **One report for the merge commit.** `speca <package> --gate-report` sums
  the package's recorded runs since a commit: full and task runs, their
  seconds, how many were reused, the full gate's duration at the baseline and
  on the last tree, and the slowest units of the last full gate.
- **af-impl calls the command.** af-impl runs every gate through
  `speca --gate`, runs the full gate only at the baseline, after the
  integration task, after the conformance fix commit and on the merged tree,
  and runs a more thorough repository target once, on the merged tree.

## Non-goals

This package is the first of nine scopes of
`docs/prd/07-keep-the-implementation-loop-fast-and-close-its-open-items.md`.
Each of the others is a package of its own:

- **`specrun_driver`**: the Go driver that replaces `scripts/impl-specs.sh`
  (PRD 5.1, 5.2, 5.7 to 5.9, 5.11 to 5.14).
- **`open_item_kinds`**: kinds, labels and counts of open items, and closing
  what a branch resolved (PRD 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.7).
- **`open_items_read_back`**: no handoff to a landed package, the survey
  reading open items, passing them on, and the `AF-Run:` trailer (PRD 3.3,
  3.4, 3.6, 5.10). Until then af-impl copies the gate report into the merge
  commit's body as prose.
- **`specrun_label_rules`** and **`specrun_repair_reconcile`** (PRD 5.3 to
  5.6, 3.8).
- **`gate_affected_tests_budget`**: `test_commands.affected_tests` with its
  `{base}` placeholder and the `--base` flag, the gate budget and the growth
  over the base branch, and the test-cost directive (PRD 1.2, 1.6, 1.7).
  Until then the task gate runs `all_tests`, and the verdict carries no
  budget.
- **`package_handoffs`** (PRD 4.1 to 4.5) and **`unattended_mode`** (PRD 2.1,
  2.2).

Also out:

- **Weakening the test-first gate.** Every task's new tests are still seen
  failing first, and every task still lands only on a passing gate.
- **Slowest units for other tools.** Only Go's test output is recognised.
  pytest files and Jest suites are later additions; for any other output the
  list is empty.
- **A change to the format.** No schema changes in this package.
- **Deciding the verdict against the baseline.** af-impl still compares the
  gate's verdict with the baseline using its own table. Only the running and
  the bookkeeping move into `speca`.

## Background

af-impl's gate is `linter`, then `all_tests`, from the package's
`test_commands`. `skills/af-impl/SKILL.md` has the model run both at the
baseline (§2), after every task and after the integration task (§5), in a
clean environment and after the conformance fixes (§6,
`references/conformance.md`), and on the merged tree (§7,
`references/landing.md`). That is 14 to 16 runs for a ten-task package.

Measured over 25 packages on one repository, the time in the gate grew from 3
to 44 minutes per package while the packages stayed the same size. Two of the
causes are in this package's reach:

- **Some runs repeat a tree that was already checked.** The baseline of
  package N+1 is the merged tree of package N. When the base branch did not
  move, the merged tree of a `--no-ff` merge is the branch tip's tree.
- **The quality command was widened per task.** The project template
  (`docs/templates/AGENTS.md`, "Quality Commands") says "where a target such
  as `check` is more thorough than the `test_commands`, run that target
  instead", so every task gate became `make check`.

Nothing records what a gate run cost, so the slowdown was seen only in wall
time, hours later.

`speca` (`cmd/speca`) already reads `test_commands` through `afspec` and is
the command af-impl calls for every other mechanical step. It has eight
forms, chosen in `cmd/speca/forms.go`, each answering in the envelope of
`envelope.AdminResult`. Today no form starts a process, and nothing in the
module writes under the user's state directory.

## Requirements

### 1. Running a gate

`speca <package> --gate task|full [--clean-env] [--timeout <duration>]` runs
one gate of the package and answers in speca's JSON envelope.

- **The commands.** Both levels run `linter`, then `all_tests`, from the
  package's `test_commands`, in the repository `--dir` names. The level is
  part of the answer and of the reuse key. (The task level gets its own
  command in `gate_affected_tests_budget`.)
- **No shell.** Each command string is split into a program and its
  arguments on white space, with single and double quotes keeping a quoted
  stretch together, and the program is started directly. A pipe, `&&`, a
  redirection or `$VAR` reaches the program as a literal argument.
- **First failure stops.** A command that exits non-zero ends the gate with
  `fail`; the commands after it do not run.
- **`not_run`.** A command that cannot start, because its program is not
  found or the package's `test_commands` name no command for it, ends the
  gate with `not_run`, with the reason.
- **A timeout.** A command still running after `--timeout` (default 20
  minutes) is ended together with the processes it started, and the gate
  ends with `fail`, marked as timed out.
- **Any status, no writes.** The gate is not a task move. It runs for a
  package in any lifecycle status and writes nothing into the repository or
  the package.
- **Exit code.** `0` when the gate ran, whatever its verdict; the verdict is
  in the JSON. `2` for a level that is neither `task` nor `full`, for a gate
  combined with another form, and for a gate flag without `--gate`.

The verdict (`result.gate`) holds: `level`; `verdict`; `clean_env`; `reused`
when the result was reused; per command its `name`, `exit_code`, `seconds`,
the path of its `log`, and for a failing command its `tail`; the total
`seconds`; and for a full gate the `slowest` units.

### 2. The clean environment

`--clean-env` runs every command of the gate with an empty temporary
directory as `HOME`, no global and no system git configuration, and
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. Everything else in the environment is inherited.
The temporary directory is removed when the gate ends. Without the flag the
commands inherit speca's environment unchanged.

### 3. Reusing a result that passed

Every gate that ends in `pass` is recorded in a file outside the repository,
under the user's state directory, keyed by four things:

- the tree id of the working tree as it is, tracked and untracked files
  included and ignored files left out, computed through a temporary index so
  that the user's index is not touched;
- the gate level;
- the exact `linter` and `all_tests` command strings;
- whether the environment was clean.

A gate whose key matches a recorded pass runs nothing and returns `pass`,
with `reused` naming the commit that was checked out and the time of the run
it came from, and that run's seconds. A `fail` or a `not_run` is never
recorded for reuse.

Two things can keep a result from being recorded, and neither stops the
gate: `--dir` is not inside a git work tree, so there is no tree id; or the
state directory cannot be written. The gate runs, answers with its verdict,
and raises a `gate_not_recorded` warning that says why.

### 4. Output and logs

Each command's full output, stdout and stderr together, goes to a log file
outside the repository, under the user's state directory. The verdict names
the file. For a failing command the verdict also holds the last 40 lines of
its output, or all of it when it is shorter, so the model reads a failure
without reading a log. None of a command's output reaches speca's stdout,
which stays one JSON object.

### 5. Measuring a gate

Every command's wall-clock seconds are recorded, and the gate's total is
their sum. For a full gate, speca reads the `all_tests` output for Go's
per-package result lines (`ok <package> <n>s`, `FAIL <package> <n>s`) and
keeps the five with the most seconds, slowest first. Lines without a
duration (`(cached)`, `[no test files]`) are not units. For an output it
does not recognise, the list is empty. A task gate carries no list.

### 6. The gate report

`speca <package> --gate-report [--since <commit>]` sums the gate runs
recorded for this package and writes nothing. A run counts when the commit
that was checked out when it ran is `--since` itself or a descendant of it
that is reachable from `HEAD` or, while a merge is uncommitted, from
`MERGE_HEAD`. Without `--since`, the commit is the merge base of `HEAD` and
the base branch: the branch `origin/HEAD` names, else `main`.

The report (`result.gate_report`) holds:

- for the full level and for the task level: the number of runs, their
  seconds, and how many were reused;
- the full gate's duration at the baseline, the earliest full run counted,
  and on the last tree, the latest one; a reused run's duration is that of
  the run it came from;
- the slowest units of the last full gate.

With no run to count, every number is zero and the list is empty. A
`--since` that names no commit, or no `--since` and no base branch to take
it from, is a usage error.

### 7. Describing the gate

`speca --schema` and the help describe the two forms and their flags. The
envelope's summary says the level, the verdict and the seconds of a gate, or
that it was reused, and for the report the runs it counted.

### 8. af-impl and the project template

These are changes to text, made in the same change as the command:

- **Two gate levels.** af-impl runs the task gate (`speca <package> --gate
  task`) after every implement task, and the full gate (`--gate full`) at
  the baseline, after the integration task, after the conformance fix commit
  when there is one, and on the merged tree. The clean-environment run of
  the conformance pass is `--gate full --clean-env`. The verdict table of
  af-impl §5 applies to both levels.
- **The gate runs the spec's commands.** A more thorough repository target,
  such as `make check`, runs once, on the merged tree, before the merge is
  committed. af-impl's text says this order takes precedence over a project
  instruction to substitute the thorough target for every check.
- **The report.** af-impl notes the commit of the baseline, and copies
  `speca <package> --gate-report --since <that commit>` into the merge
  commit's body and its own report: the full gate's duration at the baseline
  and on the merged tree, the slowest units, and the runs with how many were
  reused. A reused gate is reported as "reused the gate of `<commit>`,
  `<date>`".
- **The template.** The "Quality Commands" section of
  `docs/templates/AGENTS.md` is reworded: the thorough target before
  committing a merge, the spec's commands between tasks.

## Design Decisions

1. **The gate is a `speca` command, not instructions to the model** (PRD
   decision 16). Recording results by tree, timing runs, parsing per-unit
   times and summing runs are mechanical; as skill instructions they are
   fragile and add model turns to the path this plan makes cheaper.
2. **Reuse a gate by tree id, never by commit** (PRD decision 3). Two
   commits with the same tree are the same code. The key includes the
   commands and the environment, so a clean-environment run is never
   replaced by a normal one. Only passes are cached: a failure is cheap to
   run again and must be seen.
3. **The thorough repository target runs once, before the merge commit**
   (PRD decision 4). Formatting and tidiness cannot change a test's result,
   and the gate on the merged tree decides what lands.
4. **Both levels run `all_tests` in this package.** The PRD's sequencing
   puts `affected_tests` in a later step; the level is still recorded and
   keyed, so the later package changes one command and no caller.
   `--base` is left to that package, because without `{base}` it would do
   nothing.
5. **The budget fields are left out of the verdict.** The budget and the
   growth over the base branch belong to `gate_affected_tests_budget`; a
   field that is always absent would only mislead.
6. **A command is split on white space with quotes, and nothing else.**
   `test_commands` must need no shell features, and af-impl already checks
   that. Splitting with quotes covers `make test` and
   `go test ./... -run 'A|B'`; anything more would be a shell.
7. **A gate command times out after 20 minutes by default.** The PRD's
   driver ends a session after 30 minutes without an event and requires a
   single gate to stay below that; a hung test must end the gate, not the
   session.
8. **A gate that cannot be recorded still runs.** Outside a git work tree,
   or with a state directory that cannot be written, the verdict is still
   true; only the reuse and the report lose a run, and a warning says so.
9. **The report selects runs by ancestry, not by time.** The run log holds
   the commit checked out at each run. Counting the runs at `--since` and at
   its descendants on this branch needs no clock and survives a base branch
   that moved; `MERGE_HEAD` is included because the gate on the merged tree
   runs before the merge is committed.
10. **af-impl passes `--since`.** It knows the commit its baseline ran on.
    The default, the merge base with the base branch, is for a person.
11. **The state lives under `$XDG_STATE_HOME`, else `~/.local/state`, in
    `agent-fox/speca`.** Linux and macOS are the target platforms, and one
    directory for both keeps the docs and the tests the same.
12. **Only the template's "Quality Commands" is reworded.** The PRD names
    `docs/templates/AGENTS.md`. This repository's own `AGENTS.md` and
    `CLAUDE.md` are left as they are; af-impl's text takes precedence over
    them for the gate.
13. **The skill and template texts are task steps, not criteria.** The
    project's steering forbids a test of what a document says, so they carry
    no check; `make skills-check` holds the skill to its render rules.

## Dependencies

- `speca`'s JSON envelope and exit-code conventions (`docs/speca.md`,
  ADR 10), which both forms follow.
- `afspec`, for the package and its `test_commands`.
- `git`, for the tree id, the commit checked out and the ancestry of the
  report. No other package under the spec root: every earlier package is
  archived.
- The af-impl skill (`skills/af-impl`) and the project template
  (`docs/templates/AGENTS.md`), whose text changes.

## Glossary

- **gate**: the package's `linter` command followed by its `all_tests`
  command, run to decide whether work may land.
- **task gate**, **full gate**: the gate after an implement task, and the
  gate at the baseline, after the integration task, after the conformance
  fixes and on the merged tree.
- **baseline**: the gate on the unchanged tree, before a package's first
  task.
- **tree id**: git's hash of a directory tree's content; two trees with the
  same id hold the same files.
- **unit**: what a test tool reports a duration for; for Go, a test package.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Run a gate of the package's commands

**Rationale:** A model that runs the gate by hand repeats work and keeps the result in its head; one call with one verdict is the same every time.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN `speca <package> --gate full` is called and no passing result is recorded under the gate's key, THE speca SHALL run the package's `linter` command, then its `all_tests` command, each once, in the directory `--dir` names, and report the verdict `pass` when both exit with code 0
   → exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate` holds `level` "full", `verdict` "pass", `clean_env` false, `commands` with one entry per command in run order, each with `name` (`linter`, then `all_tests`), `exit_code` 0 and `seconds`, and the total `seconds`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a temporary git repository with one commit, holding one package under .specs whose test_commands name two executable scripts outside the repository, each appending its own name to a file outside the repository
   - setup: XDG_STATE_HOME set to an empty temporary directory
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go (new), a table over the levels {full, task}, with the helpers run and result of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', level); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.level == level and g.verdict == 'pass' and g.clean_env == false; assert names(g.commands) == ['linter', 'all_tests'] and every exit_code == 0; assert the scripts' file reads 'linter\nall_tests\n'; assert g.slowest is present for full and absent for task
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN `speca <package> --gate task` is called and no passing result is recorded under the gate's key, THE speca SHALL run the same two commands in the same order and report the verdict with `level` "task"
   → as REQ-1.1, with `level` "task"
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.3] IF a command of the gate exits with a code other than 0, THEN THE speca SHALL end the gate with the verdict `fail` and start none of the commands after it
   → exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "fail"; `commands` ends with the failing command and its `exit_code`; a command after it has no entry and was not started
   Check: integration
   - setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, with the linter script exiting 3
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'fail'; assert len(g.commands) == 1 and g.commands[0].name == 'linter' and g.commands[0].exit_code == 3; assert the all_tests script left no line in its file. A second case with linter passing and all_tests exiting 1: two entries, the second with exit_code 1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF a command cannot start: its program is not found, its command string has an unterminated quote, or the package's `test_commands` hold no `linter` or no `all_tests` command, THEN THE speca SHALL end the gate with the verdict `not_run` and start no further command
   → exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "not_run"; `result.gate.reason` names the command and says why it could not start; that command's entry, when it has one, carries no `exit_code`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {linter names a program that does not exist; all_tests names a program that does not exist (the linter script ran first); linter is `make 'lint` with the quote left open; tasks.json holds an empty test_commands object}: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'not_run'; assert g.reason contains the command's name; assert no entry of g.commands for that command has exit_code
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE speca SHALL start each command's program directly, with the arguments its command string holds when split on white space, a stretch inside single or double quotes kept as one argument without its quotes
   → the program receives `|`, `&&`, `>`, `$HOME` and `*` as literal arguments, and an argument with a space when it was quoted; no shell is started
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gate/command_test.go (new), a table over command strings for the function that splits one: 'make test' -> [make, test]; "go test ./... -run 'A|B'" -> [go, test, ./..., -run, A|B]; 'x "a b" c' -> [x, a b, c]; 'x  a\tb' -> [x, a, b]; 'x && y > z $HOME *' -> [x, &&, y, >, z, $HOME, *]; '' and '   ' -> an error; "x 'a" -> an error. One case through cmd/speca/gate_test.go: a script that writes its arguments one per line, named in all_tests as `<script> a|b '$HOME c' *`; assert its file holds exactly 'a|b', '$HOME c', '*'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF a command is still running when the time `--timeout` gives, 20 minutes when the flag is absent, has passed since it started, THEN THE speca SHALL end the command and every process it started, and end the gate with the verdict `fail`
   → exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "fail"; the command's entry has `timed_out` true and no `exit_code`; no process the command started is running when speca returns; nothing is recorded for reuse
   Check: integration
   - setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, with an all_tests script that starts a child process sleeping 60 seconds, writes both process ids to a file outside the repository and waits
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '300ms'); assert code == 0; c = last(env.result.gate.commands); assert env.result.gate.verdict == 'fail' and c.timed_out and c.exit_code is absent; assert neither recorded process id is alive; env2 = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '300ms'); assert env2.result.gate.reused is absent
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] IF `--gate` is given a value other than `task` or `full`, THEN THE speca SHALL refuse the call before a package is read or a command is started
   → exit code 2; `error.category` is "usage" and `error.fix_hint` names the flag `--gate` with the valid values `task` and `full`; nothing was run or written
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/speca/main_test.go, beside the existing table of flag combinations that are refused with a usage error, the cases {--gate '', --gate all, --gate Full}: env, code = run('09', '--gate', value); assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage'; assert env.error.fix_hint.flag == '--gate' and env.error.fix_hint.valid == ['task', 'full']
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] IF `--gate` or `--gate-report` is combined with another form (`--validate`, `--list`, `--next`, `--task` or `--state`, `--status`, `--render`, `--migrate`, or the other of the two), is given no package, or a flag is given without its form (`--clean-env` or `--timeout` without `--gate`, `--since` without `--gate-report`), or `--timeout` is not a duration greater than zero, THEN THE speca SHALL refuse the call before a package is read or a command is started
   → exit code 2 and `error.category` "usage", with a message that names the two operations or the flag and the form it needs; nothing was run or written
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/speca/main_test.go, the same table as REQ-1.7 with one case per combination the condition lists, among them ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--validate'], ['--gate', 'full'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--gate-report'], ['09', '--clean-env'], ['09', '--since', 'HEAD'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '0s'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', 'soon']: assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage' and the snapshot of the repository is as it was
   ```

### REQ-2: Run the gate in a clean environment

**Rationale:** A test that passes only on this machine's configuration fails for everyone else; the conformance pass asks for this run and should not have to build it by hand.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHERE `--clean-env` is given with `--gate`, THE speca SHALL run every command of the gate with `HOME` set to an empty directory created for this gate, with no global and no system git configuration read, and with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` set to `0`, every other environment variable inherited
   → `result.gate.clean_env` is true; a command sees a `HOME` that is an empty directory, `git config --global --list` and `git config --system --list` print nothing in it, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` is `0`, and a variable set in speca's environment is still set
   Check: integration
   - setup: HOME set to a temporary directory whose .gitconfig sets user.name, and a variable GATE_PROBE=1 in the environment
   - setup: an all_tests script that writes, to a file outside the repository, $HOME, the listing of $HOME, $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, $GATE_PROBE and the output of `git config --global --list` and `git config --system --list`
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {with --clean-env, without}: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', flag...); with the flag: assert env.result.gate.clean_env; assert the probe file shows a HOME other than the test's, an empty listing, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT == '0', GATE_PROBE == '1' and no git configuration line. Without it: assert clean_env == false, HOME is the test's and the global configuration lists user.name
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN a gate run with `--clean-env` ends, with any verdict, THE speca SHALL remove the directory it created as `HOME`, with everything the commands wrote into it
   → the directory a command saw as `HOME` does not exist when speca returns
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over an all_tests script that {exits 0, exits 1, runs past --timeout}, each writing $HOME to a file outside the repository and creating a file inside $HOME: run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env', ...); assert the recorded directory does not exist
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a gate is run without `--clean-env`, THE speca SHALL run every command with speca's own environment, unchanged
   → `result.gate.clean_env` is false; a command sees speca's `HOME` and the user's global git configuration
   Check: same as REQ-2.1

### REQ-3: Reuse a result that passed

**Rationale:** The baseline of one package is the merged tree of the one before, and a merged tree is often the branch tip's tree; running the suite on a tree that already passed buys nothing.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a gate ends with the verdict `pass` in a git work tree, THE speca SHALL record the result outside the repository, under `agent-fox/speca` in the user's state directory (`$XDG_STATE_HOME`, else `~/.local/state`), keyed by the tree id of the working tree with tracked and untracked files included and ignored files left out, the level, the exact `linter` and `all_tests` command strings, and whether the environment was clean
   → after the call a record exists under the state directory and no file is new under `--dir`; a later call with the same key is answered from it
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a gate is called and a passing result is recorded under its key, THE speca SHALL start no command and answer with the recorded pass
   → exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is "pass"; `reused` holds `commit` (the commit that was checked out at the recorded run), `at` (the time of that run, RFC 3339) and `seconds` (its total); `commands` is empty and `seconds` is 0; for a full gate `slowest` is the recorded run's
   Check: integration
   - setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, whose scripts count their runs in a file outside the repository
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: first = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert first.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran once; assert a file exists under $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/speca and the snapshot of the repository is as it was; second = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); g = second.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'pass' and g.reused.commit == rev-parse(HEAD) and g.reused.at parses as RFC 3339 and g.reused.seconds == first.result.gate.seconds; assert g.commands == [] and g.seconds == 0 and g.slowest == first.result.gate.slowest; assert the scripts still ran once
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE speca SHALL for any gate whose key differs from every recorded pass in one part (the content of a tracked file, an untracked file that is not ignored, the level, a command string, or the clean environment), run the commands
   → `result.gate.reused` is absent and both commands were started
   Check: integration
   - setup: the repository of REQ-3.2 after one passing `--gate full`, with a .gitignore that ignores *.log
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table of one change each, the gate run after it and the expected answer: {edit a tracked file -> ran; add an untracked file notes.txt -> ran; call --gate task -> ran; change the all_tests string in tasks.json by one argument -> ran; add --clean-env -> ran; add an ignored file x.log -> reused; commit the uncommitted change that the last pass covered -> reused, with reused.commit the commit before it; merge a branch with --no-ff whose tip's tree passed, the base not having moved -> reused}: assert reused is present exactly where the table says, and the scripts' run count rose exactly where it says ran
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] THE speca SHALL for any two working trees that hold the same files with the same content, use one key whatever commit is checked out and whatever the ignored files hold
   → a gate on the second tree is answered with `reused` naming the commit of the first run
   Check: same as REQ-3.3
1. [REQ-3.5] IF a gate ends with the verdict `fail` or `not_run`, THEN THE speca SHALL record nothing that a later gate could reuse
   → the next call with the same key starts the commands again and its `result.gate.reused` is absent
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {all_tests exits 1, linter names a missing program}: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == b.result.gate.verdict and b.result.gate.reused is absent; for the failing script assert it ran twice
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] THE speca SHALL work out the tree id without changing the repository: the user's index, the staged changes, the working tree and every file under `.git` stay as they were
   → with staged, unstaged and untracked changes present, every file under `--dir`, `.git` and its index and object store included, has the same content, size and mode after a gate as before it, and `git status --porcelain` prints the same
   Check: integration
   - setup: the repository of REQ-1.1 with one staged edit, one unstaged edit and one untracked file
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, with the helper snapshot of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: before = snapshot(root); status = git('status', '--porcelain'); run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert snapshot(root) == before; assert git('status', '--porcelain') == status; assert git('diff', '--cached', '--name-only') still names the staged file alone
   ```
1. [REQ-3.7] IF `--dir` is not inside a git work tree, or `git` is not installed, THEN THE speca SHALL run the gate and answer with its verdict, recording nothing
   → exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is what the commands returned; `warnings` holds one `gate_not_recorded` entry whose message says there is no tree id to record the result under; a second call starts the commands again
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {a directory with .specs and no .git, a repository with PATH holding no git}: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.exit_code == 0 and a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass'; assert codes(a.warnings) == ['gate_not_recorded']; b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert b.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran twice
   ```
1. [REQ-3.8] IF the state directory cannot be created or written, or a recorded result under the gate's key cannot be parsed, THEN THE speca SHALL run the gate and answer with its verdict
   → exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is what the commands returned; where the directory cannot be written, `warnings` holds one `gate_not_recorded` entry naming the path and each command's `log` is absent; where a record cannot be parsed, it counts as no record, and the pass replaces it
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, two cases. XDG_STATE_HOME names a regular file: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.exit_code == 0 and a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and codes(a.warnings) == ['gate_not_recorded'] and the warning's message contains the path; assert no command entry has log. A recorded pass overwritten with 'not json': b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert b.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran; c = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert c.result.gate.reused is present
   ```

### REQ-4: Keep a command's output in a log and its failure in the verdict

**Rationale:** A test suite's output is thousands of lines the model does not need; the forty that explain a failure are the ones it does.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a command of the gate runs, THE speca SHALL write everything the command prints to stdout and stderr to one log file of its own under the state directory, and name the file in the command's `log`
   → `log` is an absolute path that is not under `--dir`; the file holds the command's complete output
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: with a linter script printing 'out-1' to stdout and 'err-1' to stderr and an all_tests script printing 3000 numbered lines: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); for each c of env.result.gate.commands: assert c.log is absolute and not under root and under $XDG_STATE_HOME; assert read(commands[0].log) contains 'out-1' and 'err-1'; assert read(commands[1].log) holds all 3000 lines in order; assert the two paths differ
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF a command exits with a code other than 0 or is ended by the timeout, THEN THE speca SHALL put the last 40 lines of the command's output in its `tail`
   → `tail` holds the last 40 lines of the output in order, all of them when the output has fewer, and is an empty string when the command printed nothing; a command that exited with 0 has no `tail`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over a failing all_tests script that prints {0, 1, 40, 41, 500} numbered lines, and one that prints 41 lines with no newline after the last: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); c = last(env.result.gate.commands); assert lines(c.tail) == the last min(n, 40) lines printed, in order; assert the passing linter's entry has no tail
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE speca SHALL keep everything a command prints off its own stdout
   → speca's stdout is exactly one JSON object, whatever the commands print and however much
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: with a linter script that prints '{"ok":false}' and an all_tests script that prints 5 MB: out = the bytes speca wrote to stdout for ['NN', '--gate', 'full']; assert json.decode(out) succeeds with nothing left over; assert out does not contain the scripts' text
   ```

### REQ-5: Measure what a gate costs

**Rationale:** The suite of the measured run grew from ten seconds to nearly three minutes and nobody noticed, because nothing wrote a duration down.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE speca SHALL record the wall-clock seconds each command of a gate ran, and report the gate's total as their sum
   → each `commands[i].seconds` is a number of seconds, zero or more, to the millisecond; `result.gate.seconds` equals their sum
   Check: unit
   - setup: the gate runner's clock replaced by one that advances 1.5 s during the first command and 2.25 s during the second
   ```
   in internal/gate/run_test.go (new): r = run the gate with two commands that exit 0; assert r.commands[0].seconds == 1.5 and r.commands[1].seconds == 2.25 and r.seconds == 3.75
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN the `all_tests` command of a full gate has run and its output holds Go's per-package result lines, THE speca SHALL report the five packages with the most seconds, slowest first, as `slowest`
   → `slowest` holds at most five entries `{unit, seconds}`, ordered by seconds descending, entries with equal seconds in output order; a line `ok <package> <n>s` or `FAIL <package> <n>s` is a unit, with or without text after the duration; a line with `(cached)` or `[no test files]` is not
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/gate/units_test.go (new), a table over outputs for the function that reads the units: {no line -> []; three ok lines -> three entries, slowest first; seven lines, one of them FAIL -> the five slowest, the FAIL line among them when its seconds place it; 'ok  \tpkg/a\t(cached)' and '?   \tpkg/b\t[no test files]' -> not units; 'ok  \tpkg/c\t0.512s\tcoverage: 81.0% of statements' -> {pkg/c, 0.512}; two lines of 1.000s -> output order; pytest and Jest output -> []}
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN the `all_tests` command of a full gate has run and its output holds no line speca recognises, THE speca SHALL report an empty list of slowest units
   → `result.gate.slowest` is present and is `[]`
   Check: same as REQ-5.2
1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN a task gate has run, THE speca SHALL report no list of slowest units
   → `result.gate.slowest` is absent
   Check: same as REQ-1.1

### REQ-6: Sum a package's gate runs for the merge commit

**Rationale:** The merge commit and the report must say what the gates cost from something that was measured, not from what a model remembers.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN `speca <package> --gate-report --since <commit>` is called, THE speca SHALL count the gate runs recorded for this package that ended in `pass` or `fail`, reused ones included, whose checked-out commit is `<commit>` or a descendant of it reachable from `HEAD` or, while a merge is uncommitted, from `MERGE_HEAD`
   → exit code 0; `result.gate_report` holds `since` (the full id of the commit) and, under `full` and under `task`, `runs`, `seconds` (the sum of the runs' own seconds, a reused run adding 0) and `reused`; a run of another package, a `not_run` gate and a run at a commit outside that range are not counted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a repository with two packages and the commits B (base), then F1, F2 and F3 on a branch, and a commit X on another branch
   - setup: gates run through speca itself: package one full at B, task at F1, task again at F1 (reused), full failing at F2, full passing at F3, which commits the fix; package two full at B; package one full at X; package one full with a missing linter program at F3
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go (new): on F3: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report', '--since', B); r = env.result.gate_report; assert env.exit_code == 0 and r.since == B; assert r.full.runs == 3 and r.full.reused == 0; assert r.task.runs == 2 and r.task.reused == 1; assert r.full.seconds == the sum of the three full runs' seconds as their verdicts reported them. Then on the base, after `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <branch>` and one more `--gate full`: assert the report counts 4 full runs and full.reused == 1, the merged tree being F3's
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] THE speca SHALL report the duration of the earliest full run counted as `baseline_full_seconds`, that of the latest as `last_full_seconds`, a reused run's duration being that of the run it came from, and the slowest units of the latest full run as `slowest`
   → `baseline_full_seconds` and `last_full_seconds` are numbers of seconds; `slowest` is the list the latest full run's verdict held, the recorded run's list when that run was reused
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, in the scenario of the test above with an all_tests script that prints two Go result lines: assert r.baseline_full_seconds == the seconds of the full gate at B; assert r.last_full_seconds == the seconds of the passing full gate at F3; after the reused gate on the merged tree: assert r.last_full_seconds is still that number and not 0, and r.slowest == the two units, slowest first
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] IF no recorded run counts: the state directory holds no run of this package in the range, or no run log at all, or only lines that cannot be parsed, THEN THE speca SHALL report a count of zero for every number
   → exit code 0; `full` and `task` each hold `runs` 0, `seconds` 0 and `reused` 0; `baseline_full_seconds` and `last_full_seconds` are absent; `slowest` is `[]`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {an empty state directory, a run log holding one run of another package, a run log holding 'not json' and one run of this package (that run is counted, the line skipped)}: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report', '--since', 'HEAD'); assert env.exit_code == 0; for the first two: assert every count is 0, both durations are absent and slowest == []; for the third: assert full.runs == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHEN `speca <package> --gate-report` is called without `--since`, THE speca SHALL take as the commit the merge base of `HEAD` and the base branch, which is the branch `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` names, else `main`
   → `result.gate_report.since` is the full id of that merge base, and the runs are counted from it
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {a clone whose origin/HEAD names a branch trunk, a repository with no remote and a branch main}: on a feature branch two commits ahead: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report'); assert env.result.gate_report.since == git('merge-base', 'HEAD', base)
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] IF `--since` names no commit of the repository, or `--since` is absent and neither `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` nor a branch `main` exists, or `--dir` is not inside a git work tree, THEN THE speca SHALL refuse the call
   → exit code 2 and `error.category` "usage"; the message names the value that is no commit, or says to give `--since <commit>`, or says the directory is not a git work tree; there is no `result`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {--since nosuchref; no --since in a repository whose only branch is work; a directory with .specs and no .git}: env, code = run('<one>', '--gate-report', ...); assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage' and env.result is absent; assert env.error.message contains 'nosuchref', '--since' or 'git' as the case has it
   ```

### REQ-7: Leave the repository alone and describe the two forms

**Rationale:** A gate is a measurement, not a task move, and an agent learns a command from its own description.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] THE speca SHALL for any lifecycle status of the package (draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived), run `--gate` and `--gate-report` and leave every file and directory under `--dir` as it was
   → the gate answers with a verdict and the report with its counts in every status; no file under `--dir`, the package's `progress.json` and `spec.md` and the `.git` directory included, is created, changed or removed
   Check: integration
   - setup: a git repository with one package per status, the superseded and archived ones under .specs/archive and named by their path, each with passing scripts that write outside the repository
   ```
   in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over the five statuses, with the helpers packageWith and snapshot of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: before = snapshot(root); a = run(ref, '--gate', 'full'); b = run(ref, '--gate', 'task'); c = run(ref, '--gate-report', '--since', 'HEAD'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and b.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and c.result.gate_report.full.runs == 1; assert snapshot(root) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN `speca --schema` is called, THE speca SHALL describe the flags `--gate` with its two values, `--clean-env`, `--timeout`, `--gate-report` and `--since`, and the result fields `gate` and `gate_report` with every field of each
   → the JSON document's `flags` holds the five flags, `gate` with the enumeration `task`, `full`; its `result` schema holds `gate` and `gate_report` with a description for every field
   Check: unit
   ```
   extends TestSchema_DescribesTheFormsFlagsAndResult in cmd/speca/schema_test.go: assert flags has gate, clean-env, timeout, gate-report and since; assert flags.gate.enum == ['task', 'full']; assert result.properties.result has gate and gate_report, and that every property under each has a description. TestSchema_MatchesTheGoldenFile in the same file compares the document with cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json, which is written again
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] THE speca SHALL say in the envelope's `summary` the level, the verdict and the seconds of a gate, or the commit a reused pass came from, and for the report the runs it counted
   → `speca: <directory> <level> gate <verdict> in <n>s` for a gate that ran; `speca: <directory> <level> gate pass, reused from <short commit>` for a reused one; `speca: <directory> <level> gate not_run: <reason>` for one that could not start; `speca: <directory> gate report: <n> full, <m> task, <k> reused` for the report
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/speca/result_test.go, beside the existing tests of Result.Summary, a table over results holding a gate {full pass 42.5 s, task fail 3 s, full pass reused from abc1234, full not_run with a reason} and a gate report {3 full, 9 task, 2 reused}: assert r.Summary() equals the sentence the contract gives for each
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An implementer gates a tree, gates it again unchanged, and reads the report

1. **implementer** runs `speca <package> --gate full` on the unchanged base branch, the baseline
2. **speca** asks git for the tree id of the working tree through a temporary index and finds no recorded pass under the key
3. **speca** runs `linter`, then `all_tests`, writing each command's output to its log and timing it
4. **gate store** records the pass under the key and the run in the package's run log
5. **implementer** commits a change on a branch and runs `speca <package> --gate task`, runs `--gate full` on the branch tip, then merges the branch with `--no-ff --no-commit` and runs `--gate full` on the merged tree
6. **speca** runs the commands for the changed tree, and for the merged tree answers `pass` with `reused`, because its tree is the branch tip's and that tree passed a full gate
7. **implementer** runs `speca <package> --gate-report --since <baseline commit>` and copies the counts into the merge commit

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** speca's Main, git, the gate's commands as real processes, the state directory on disk

**Setup:**

- a temporary git repository with a branch main and one package whose test_commands name two executable scripts that count their runs outside the repository, the all_tests script printing two Go result lines
- XDG_STATE_HOME set to an empty temporary directory

**End state:**

- the scripts ran for the baseline, for the task gate and for the full gate on the branch tip, and not for the merged tree
- the gate on the merged tree answers `pass` with `reused.commit` the branch tip
- the report counts three full runs with one reused and one task run, and holds the baseline's duration and two slowest units
- the repository holds no file the gates wrote

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/speca/e2e_test.go, beside TestAnAgentFollowsNextFromTheReportToTheFinishedTask: base = rev-parse(main); run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); switch -c feature; write and commit a file; run(pkg, '--gate', 'task'); full = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); tip = rev-parse(HEAD); switch main; merge --no-ff --no-commit feature; merged = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); assert merged.result.gate.reused.commit == tip and the run count did not rise; rep = run(pkg, '--gate-report', '--since', base).result.gate_report; assert rep.full.runs == 3 and rep.full.reused == 1 and rep.task.runs == 1 and len(rep.slowest) == 2 and rep.baseline_full_seconds is present; assert git('status', '--porcelain') lists only the merge's own changes
```

### PATH-2: A conformance pass runs the gate in a clean environment and reads the failure from the verdict

1. **implementer** runs `speca <package> --gate full --clean-env` on a branch whose tests pass on this machine
2. **speca** creates an empty directory, runs the commands with it as `HOME`, with no global or system git configuration and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`
3. **speca** sees `all_tests` exit non-zero, stops, puts the last 40 lines of its output in the verdict and removes the directory
4. **gate store** records the run in the run log and no pass to reuse
5. **implementer** reads the failure from `tail`, without opening the log, and runs the same call again after the fix

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** speca's Main, git, the gate's commands as real processes, the state directory on disk

**Setup:**

- a temporary git repository with one package whose all_tests script exits 0 when `git config --global user.name` prints a name and otherwise prints 60 lines and exits 1
- HOME set to a temporary directory whose .gitconfig sets user.name

**End state:**

- the gate without `--clean-env` answers `pass`
- the gate with `--clean-env` on the same tree is not reused, answers `fail`, and its `tail` holds the last 40 of the 60 lines
- a second gate with `--clean-env` runs the commands again
- the temporary `HOME` is gone

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/speca/e2e_test.go: a = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass'; b = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env'); g = b.result.gate; assert g.reused is absent and g.verdict == 'fail' and g.clean_env; assert lines(last(g.commands).tail) == lines 21 to 60; c = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env'); assert c.result.gate.reused is absent; assert the HOME the script recorded does not exist
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `make test`
- **linter:** `make lint`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./cmd/speca/... ./internal/gate/... ./envelope/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

None: this spec depends on no other spec.

## Tasks

### 1. Run the gate's commands and answer with a verdict (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-5.1, REQ-5.4

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the task's behaviours as tests and confirm they fail: the command splitting and the timing with a stubbed clock in the new package internal/gate, the gate form through speca's Main in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, and the refused flag combinations in the existing usage table of cmd/speca/main_test.go. The test scripts are executable files written to a temporary directory outside the repository
- 1.2 Add the package internal/gate with no import of internal/cli or of anything that depends on agentkit-go: a function that splits a command string into a program and its arguments on white space, keeping a stretch in single or double quotes as one argument and refusing an empty string and an unterminated quote; and a runner that starts each command directly in a given directory with a given environment, measures its wall-clock seconds through a clock a test can replace, stops at the first command that exits non-zero, and returns per command its name, exit code and seconds, with the total as their sum
- 1.3 A command whose program is not found, whose string cannot be split, or that test_commands does not name ends the run as not_run with a reason naming the command; no later command starts
- 1.4 Give every command a time limit: when it passes, end the command together with every process it started (start it in a process group of its own and signal the group), mark the command timed_out with no exit code, and end the run as fail
- 1.5 Add the result types to the envelope package beside AdminResult: the gate verdict (level, verdict, clean_env, reason, reused, commands, seconds, slowest) and its command entry (name, exit_code as a pointer so that 0 is written, seconds, log, tail, timed_out), each field with a description tag as the other result types carry; add the field gate to AdminResult
- 1.6 Add the gate form to cmd/speca in a file of its own, chosen in forms.go: flags --gate (task or full), --clean-env and --timeout (a Go duration, default 20m); it locates and loads the package as the report does, whatever its status, reads linter and all_tests from its test_commands, runs them in the --dir directory, and returns the verdict with exit code 0 for pass, fail and not_run alike. Both levels run the same two commands; a full gate's slowest is an empty list for now and a task gate has none
- 1.7 Refuse as a usage error, before anything is read: a --gate value other than task or full, with a fix hint naming the two values; --gate combined with another form or given no package; --clean-env or --timeout without --gate; a --timeout that is not a duration greater than zero. Extend the existing checks of options.check so that the other forms refuse --gate the way they refuse one another
- 1.8 Keep the command's output off speca's stdout from the first version on: discard it here; the next task sends it to a log

**Touches:**

- `internal/gate/`
- `cmd/speca/gate.go`
- `cmd/speca/gate_test.go`
- `cmd/speca/main.go`
- `cmd/speca/main_test.go`
- `cmd/speca/forms.go`
- `cmd/speca/helpers_test.go`
- `envelope/gate_result.go`
- `envelope/admin_result.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes

### 2. Keep each command's output in a log, a failure's tail in the verdict, and offer the clean environment (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4, REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the task's behaviours to cmd/speca/gate_test.go and confirm they fail: the log of each command, the tail table over 0, 1, 40, 41 and 500 lines, the one JSON object on stdout, the clean-environment probe with and without the flag, and the removal of the temporary HOME after a pass, a failure and a timeout
- 2.2 Resolve the state directory in internal/gate: agent-fox/speca under $XDG_STATE_HOME when it is set, else under .local/state in the user's home directory, on Linux and macOS alike
- 2.3 Send each command's stdout and stderr, together, to a log file of its own under the state directory, in a directory per repository, named so that two gates and two commands never share a file; put its absolute path in the command's log. When the file cannot be created the command still runs and its entry has no log
- 2.4 For a command that exits non-zero or times out, keep the last 40 lines of its output as it is written and put them in tail: all lines when there are fewer, an empty string when there are none, a last line without a newline counted as a line. A command that exits 0 has no tail. Do not read the whole log back into memory to find them
- 2.5 With --clean-env, create an empty temporary directory outside the repository and run every command with HOME set to it, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointing at the null device, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM set to 1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT set to 0, every other variable inherited; set clean_env in the verdict; remove the directory when the gate ends, whatever its verdict, a timeout included
- 2.6 Without --clean-env the commands inherit speca's environment unchanged

**Touches:**

- `internal/gate/`
- `cmd/speca/gate.go`
- `cmd/speca/gate_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes

### 3. Record a passing gate by tree and reuse it (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the task's behaviours to cmd/speca/gate_test.go and confirm they fail: the second call that runs nothing, the table of changes that do and do not change the key, the failure and the not_run that are never reused, the repository snapshot with staged, unstaged and untracked changes, the directory with no git, and the state directory that cannot be written or holds a record that cannot be parsed. The tests build their git repositories with a helper added to cmd/speca/helpers_test.go that sets the identity and the default branch itself, so that they pass in a clean environment
- 3.2 Work out the tree id of the working tree with git, tracked and untracked files included and ignored files left out, without touching the repository: a copy of the index in a temporary file as the index, and a temporary object directory with the repository's object store as an alternate, so that neither .git/index nor .git/objects gains or changes a file; remove both temporaries afterwards
- 3.3 Build the key from the tree id, the level, the exact linter and all_tests strings and whether the environment is clean. Before running, look the key up in the store under the state directory, in the directory of this repository; a recorded pass is returned as the verdict with reused holding the commit that was checked out at the recorded run, its time in RFC 3339 and its seconds, with commands empty, seconds 0 and, for a full gate, the recorded slowest list
- 3.4 After a gate that ends in pass, write the record through a temporary file that is renamed, holding the commit checked out, the time, the seconds and the slowest list. A fail and a not_run write no record
- 3.5 Where --dir is not inside a git work tree or git is not installed, run the gate without a lookup, record nothing and raise a gate_not_recorded warning saying there is no tree id; where the state directory cannot be created or written, run the gate, and raise the same warning naming the path. Add the warning code to envelope/warn.go and internal/cli/warn.go beside the existing ones
- 3.6 A record that cannot be parsed counts as no record: the gate runs, and a pass replaces it

### 4. Keep the slowest units of a full gate and sum a package's runs in the gate report (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5.2, REQ-5.3, REQ-6, REQ-7.1

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the task's behaviours as tests and confirm they fail: the table of test outputs for the unit reader in internal/gate, the report scenarios in the new cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, and in cmd/speca/gate_test.go the table over the five lifecycle statuses that runs both forms and compares the repository snapshot
- 4.2 Read the all_tests output of a full gate for Go's per-package result lines as it is written: a line that starts with ok or FAIL and holds a package and a duration in seconds is a unit, with or without text after the duration; a line with (cached) or [no test files] is not. Keep the five units with the most seconds, slowest first, equal ones in output order; an output with no such line gives an empty list. Put the list in the verdict's slowest and in the record of a pass
- 4.3 Append every gate that ends in pass or fail, a reused one included, to a run log under the state directory, in the directory of this repository: the package's spec id, the time, the commit checked out, the level, whether the environment was clean, the verdict, whether it was reused and from which run, its seconds, the recorded run's seconds when reused, and the slowest list. A not_run gate is not logged. A run log that cannot be written raises gate_not_recorded and does not change the verdict
- 4.4 Add the gate report form to cmd/speca in a file of its own: flags --gate-report and --since; add the report type to the envelope package and the field gate_report to AdminResult. It locates and loads the package whatever its status and writes nothing
- 4.5 Resolve the commit: --since when given; else the merge base of HEAD and the base branch, which is the branch refs/remotes/origin/HEAD names, else main. Refuse as a usage error, with no result: a --since that names no commit, no --since and no base branch, a --dir outside a git work tree, --since without --gate-report, and --gate-report combined with another form or given no package
- 4.6 Count the runs of this package whose commit is the resolved commit or a descendant of it reachable from HEAD or, when .git holds a MERGE_HEAD, from MERGE_HEAD. For the full and the task level report runs, seconds (the runs' own, a reused run adding 0) and reused; report baseline_full_seconds from the earliest full run counted and last_full_seconds from the latest, a reused run giving the seconds of the run it came from; report the latest full run's slowest list. Skip a line of the run log that cannot be parsed. With nothing to count, every number is 0, the two durations are absent and slowest is an empty list
- 4.7 Confirm that neither form writes under --dir in any lifecycle status: no progress.json, no spec.md, nothing under .git
